intent: Medical-history reveal told like a newsreel: place, date, the man, the number of days, then the body fact nobody knows.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: The FIRST human heart transplant happened in which country?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: The first human heart transplant happened in which country?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat
lines.text: United States, South Africa, or United Kingdom?
South Africa. Cape Town, December 1967: surgeon Christiaan Barnard gave Louis Washkansky a new heart.

lines.direction: hold on Cape Town; the day counter climbs to 18 and stops dead on 'pneumonia'
lines.text: The patient lived 18 days. The heart worked; it was pneumonia that killed him.

lines.direction: pull out to the Atlantic: the United States lights up on 'Stanford', then Barnard's photograph rises out of South Africa on 'first'
lines.text: Stanford had done the research, but Barnard got there first, and was famous overnight.

lines.direction: back to South Africa; the anatomical heart sticker lands on 'nerve', the brain on 'brain', the NO NERVES card on 'own', the heart pulses on 'pacemaker'
lines.text: A transplanted heart has no nerves linking it to the brain. It beats on its own pacemaker, inside the muscle.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Not where you thought. Follow us.
